fact: Decree 54 of September 2022 makes spreading falsehoods by electronic means an offence; an amendment replacing jail with fines of 10,000 to 20,000 dinars for first offences took effect on 2026-09-30, per Al Jazeera.
The journalists' union SNJT recorded six prosecutions of journalists under Decree 54 between April 2025 and April 2026.
Tunisia's National Guard spokesperson said most of the 2,000 cybercrime cases since the start of 2024 were referred to the courts, leading to detention warrants against several defendants.

CPJ describes Decree-Law 54 as Tunisia's cybercrime law, under which prosecutions of journalists proceeded in 2026.
CPJ says Ghassen Ben Khelifa was sentenced to two years on 30 March 2026 under Decree-Law 54 for false news and harming public security.
CPJ reports a run of Decree-Law 54 convictions from July 2025 to 2026, including Ramla Dahmani, Khaoula Boukrim (four years, 26 February 2026), Ben Khelifa and Sonia Dahmani.
